fact: A keyboard is an input device that sends key events to software.
A mouse translates hand movement into pointer movement on a screen.
A monitor displays visual output from a computer.
A CPU executes program instructions and performs arithmetic and logical operations.
System RAM holds working data and usually loses its contents when power is removed.
A hard drive stores data magnetically on rotating platters.
Flash memory retains stored data without continuous power.
A router forwards packets between networks.
Twisted-pair Ethernet cables carry network data over copper wires.
A server provides services or resources to other computers.
A printer converts digital documents into physical output.
A webcam captures video for a computer or network application.
A database organizes information so software can retrieve and update it.
A firewall permits or blocks network traffic according to rules.
Cloud computing delivers computing resources over a network.
Binary represents numbers using only the digits zero and one.
A flowchart uses connected shapes to show steps and decisions in a process.
A motherboard connects the processor, memory and other computer components.
A laptop combines a screen, keyboard, battery and computer in a portable enclosure.
A tablet is a portable computer commonly operated through a touchscreen.
A smartphone combines mobile communication with general-purpose computing.
Headphones convert electrical audio signals into sound near the ears.
A microphone converts sound waves into an electrical signal.
A speaker converts an audio signal into sound waves.
A digital camera records images using an electronic image sensor.
A document scanner converts physical pages into digital images.
A gamepad sends button and directional inputs to a game.
A joystick measures the direction or displacement of a control stick.
A projector casts an enlarged image onto a separate surface.
Optical drives use lasers to read patterns on compatible discs.
A memory card is a removable storage device that uses flash memory.
A rechargeable battery stores energy for use when external power is unavailable.
A power plug connects equipment to an electrical supply.
Computer fans move air to carry heat away from components.
A power button signals a device to change its power state.
An Ethernet port provides a physical connection for a network cable.
Wi-Fi connects compatible devices to a local network using radio waves.
Bluetooth supports short-range wireless communication between devices.
A dish antenna focuses radio signals to or from a satellite.
Cellular base stations provide radio coverage for mobile devices.
A computer network allows connected devices to exchange data.
The Web is a system of linked resources accessed using web technologies.
Email transfers messages between users through mail systems.
Chat software lets people exchange short messages electronically.
Video calls transmit audio and images between participants.
A search tool helps locate information matching a query.
A folder organizes files and other folders in a file system.
A file is a named collection of data stored by a file system.
A text document stores written information as digital characters.
Image files encode visual information such as pixels or vector shapes.
A video file stores a sequence of frames, often together with audio.
An audio file stores encoded sound for later playback.
An archive combines files into a container and may also compress them.
A recycle bin can retain deleted files temporarily so they may be restored.
Downloading transfers data from another system to your device.
Uploading transfers data from your device to another system.
Saving writes the current data to storage.
Copying places a duplicate of selected content on the clipboard.
Cutting prepares selected content to be moved through the clipboard.
The clipboard temporarily holds content copied or cut by the user.
Undo reverses a supported recent editing action.
Redo reapplies an action that was previously undone.
Zooming in enlarges the displayed view without necessarily changing stored data.
Zooming out shows a larger area of a document or image at once.
A lock symbol commonly indicates that access or editing is restricted.
A key symbol often represents a credential or permission used to obtain access.
Shield symbols commonly represent protective security features.
Fingerprint recognition is one method of biometric authentication.
Password masking hides entered characters from nearby observers.
A QR code encodes data in a two-dimensional pattern readable by cameras.
A barcode represents data using a machine-readable visual pattern.
A location marker identifies a position on a digital map.
Calendar applications organize dates, events and reminders.
Computer clocks help applications measure time and schedule actions.
A calculator application performs numerical operations.
Presentation software arranges content into slides for an audience.
A spreadsheet organizes data in cells and can calculate results using formulas.
A bar chart compares values using the lengths of rectangular bars.
A digital brush applies marks to an image or canvas.
A pencil icon commonly indicates drawing or editing.
A color palette helps users choose or organize colors.
Cropping removes outer portions of an image from the displayed composition.
Settings allow users to configure supported application behavior.
A terminal provides a text interface for interacting with a command-line program.
Source code contains instructions written in a programming language.
A software bug is a defect that can cause incorrect behavior.
Many programming languages use curly braces to group blocks or represent structures.
Square brackets are used for indexing or collection syntax in many languages.
A hyperlink connects a resource to another location or resource.
A browser bookmark saves a reference to a page for later access.
Notifications draw attention to events or changes in an application.
A user account associates an identity with access and preferences.
User groups can organize people who share permissions or responsibilities.
A contact list stores details used to reach people.
Refreshing requests or reconstructs the current view using updated information.
Help interfaces explain how to use a product or resolve common questions.
An information icon points to explanatory details.
Signing in establishes an authenticated session for an account.
Signing out ends the active authenticated session in an application.
An orderly shutdown closes operating-system activity before powering down.
HTML describes the structure and meaning of web content.
CSS controls the presentation of structured documents.
JavaScript can respond to user events and update web pages.
Python uses indentation to delimit blocks of code.
SQL is used to define, query and modify relational data.
JSON represents data using objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans and null.
XML uses nested tags to encode structured information.
CSV represents tabular data using delimited text records.
A Boolean value has one of two logical states: true or false.
A variable provides a name through which a program can refer to a value.
An array stores an ordered sequence of values accessible by index.
An object can group related values under named properties.
A function groups reusable instructions and can accept inputs and return a result.
A loop repeats a block of code while its continuation rule permits.
A conditional selects a branch based on a Boolean expression.
A recursive function calls itself on a smaller problem and needs a stopping condition.
A stack removes the most recently added item first.
A queue normally removes items in the order they were added.
A linked list connects elements through references to subsequent elements.
Each node in a binary tree has at most two children.
A hash table uses a hash function to map keys to storage locations.
An algorithm is a finite description of steps for solving a problem.
Sorting arranges items according to a chosen order.
Linear search checks items in sequence until it finds a match or reaches the end.
Binary search repeatedly halves the search interval in sorted data.
In a star topology, devices connect through a central point.
A bus topology connects devices along a shared communication backbone.
A ring topology connects nodes in a closed loop.
A mesh topology provides multiple interconnections between nodes.
An IP address identifies a network interface for communication over IP.
DNS resolves domain names to records such as IP addresses.
DHCP can automatically lease IP configuration to a device.
TCP provides a reliable, ordered byte stream between endpoints.
UDP sends datagrams without providing TCP-style delivery or ordering guarantees.
HTTP defines request and response semantics for web resources.
HTTPS uses TLS to protect HTTP communication in transit.
A URL describes a resource location and how to access it.
A VPN creates a protected virtual connection across another network.
A proxy acts as an intermediary for requests between a client and another server.
A load balancer distributes incoming work across multiple service instances.
An Ethernet switch forwards frames using learned MAC-address information.
A wireless access point connects wireless clients to a network.
An IPv4 subnet mask distinguishes network bits from host bits.
Transport port numbers distinguish services or communication endpoints on a host.
A packet carries a portion of data together with protocol information used for delivery.
Client-server systems separate service requesters from service providers.
Peer-to-peer systems allow participants to act as both resource providers and consumers.
A cache stores reusable results or data to reduce repeated retrieval work.
HTTP cookies store small pieces of state that a browser can send with matching requests.
A session associates multiple interactions with an ongoing user context.
Password hashing stores a one-way derived value; password-specific algorithms can slow guessing attacks.
Encryption transforms plaintext into ciphertext using an algorithm and key.
Phishing attempts to trick people into disclosing information or taking unsafe actions.
Malware is software designed to perform harmful or unauthorized actions.
Ransomware may block access to files or systems and demand payment.
Multi-factor authentication combines evidence from distinct factor categories.
A backup is a separate copy of data intended to support recovery.
Version control records changes so earlier states can be compared or recovered.
A Git branch is a movable reference to a commit.
A merge combines development histories, potentially requiring conflict resolution.
A Git commit records a snapshot together with metadata and references to parent commits.
A unit test checks a small unit of behavior against an expected result.
A debugger can pause execution and inspect variables and control flow.
An exception transfers control from normal execution to an applicable handler.
An API defines how software components can request functionality or exchange data.
REST is an architectural style whose constraints include a uniform interface and stateless interactions.
CRUD groups four basic persistent-data operations: create, read, update and delete.
A primary key uniquely identifies rows and does not allow null key values.
A foreign key constrains references to matching values in another key.
An index is an auxiliary data structure that can speed up suitable queries.
A transaction groups work that can be committed together or rolled back.
Normalization organizes relational data to reduce certain redundancies and update anomalies.
Containers isolate processes while normally sharing the host operating-system kernel.
A virtual machine runs a guest environment on virtualized hardware.
An operating system manages hardware resources and provides services for programs.
A B-tree keeps keys sorted in balanced multiway nodes, making it useful for storage indexes.
Red-black trees use color and structural rules to keep search paths logarithmic in size.
An AVL tree maintains a height difference of at most one between each node's subtrees.
A min-heap keeps each parent's key no greater than its children's keys.
A trie stores strings along shared prefix paths.
Breadth-first search explores a graph by increasing edge distance from the start.
Depth-first search follows a path deeply before backtracking to explore alternatives.
Dijkstra's algorithm finds shortest paths when edge weights are nonnegative.
A-star prioritizes nodes using a known path cost plus a heuristic estimate of remaining cost.
Quicksort partitions elements around a pivot and recursively sorts the partitions.
Merge sort divides a sequence and combines sorted subsequences.
Dynamic programming reuses solutions to overlapping subproblems.
Memoization stores results of function calls so repeated inputs can reuse them.
Big O notation describes an asymptotic upper bound on growth.
A race condition occurs when behavior depends on the timing of concurrent operations.
A deadlock can arise when tasks hold resources while cyclically waiting for one another.
A mutex restricts access to a protected region to one owner at a time.
A counting semaphore controls access using a count of available permits.
A thread pool reuses workers to execute queued tasks.
The JavaScript event loop coordinates queued work when the call stack is available.
A Promise represents an eventual result and settles by fulfillment or rejection.
A closure retains access to its lexical environment after the outer function returns.
JavaScript object lookup can follow the prototype chain when a property is not found locally.
Polymorphism lets different implementations respond through a common interface.
Dependency injection supplies a component's dependencies from outside it.
The observer pattern notifies registered dependents when a subject changes.
The singleton pattern restricts a class to one instance and provides access to it.
A factory centralizes creation of objects behind a common creation interface.
Under a network partition, a distributed system cannot guarantee both linearizable consistency and availability for every request.
ACID describes transaction properties: atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability.
MVCC lets transactions observe suitable versions of data rather than always blocking one another.
Optimistic concurrency checks whether data changed before accepting an update.
Pessimistic locking reserves access before performing conflicting work.
Two-phase commit first prepares participants, then tells them to commit or abort.
Raft organizes replicated state around elected leaders and replicated logs.
With no new updates and successful propagation, eventually consistent replicas converge.
Sharding partitions a dataset across storage nodes.
Replication maintains copies of data on multiple nodes.
Write-ahead logging records recovery information before the corresponding data-page changes are persisted.
A database execution plan describes operations used to produce a query result.
SQL injection occurs when untrusted input is interpreted as part of a SQL command; parameterized queries separate data from code.
Cross-site scripting lets untrusted content execute as script in another user's browser.
CSRF tricks a signed-in browser into sending an unintended request to another site.
A signed compact JWT commonly has base64url-encoded header, payload and signature segments.
Public-key cryptography uses mathematically related public and private keys.
A digital signature allows a verifier to check message integrity and the signer's possession of a private key.
A TLS handshake negotiates connection parameters and establishes traffic keys.
A zero-knowledge proof demonstrates a statement without revealing additional knowledge beyond its validity.
A Merkle tree combines child hashes so a root hash commits to the underlying data.
A Bloom filter can report false positives, but a standard correctly maintained filter has no false negatives for inserted items.
